reason: I want to follow fuel toward usable energy, starting with glucose and oxygen entering the mitochondria.
expectation: I expect a product representing energy released from glucose, though it may require another step to make ATP.

alternatives.reason: The filaments look relevant to pulling, but I want to follow the energy supply first.

effect: Glucose is split in the cell fluid before smaller fuel molecules enter the mitochondrion. I can now follow the fuel toward ATP.
reaction: The split before entry was a useful detail.
reason: ADP and phosphate seem like the next ingredients for making ATP.
expectation: I expect the fuelled mitochondria to help turn ADP and phosphate into ATP.

alternatives.reason: The filaments should contribute to pulling, but I want to finish the energy supply first.

effect: The mitochondria produced an ATP supply, and the returning ADP and phosphate show how the cell can keep remaking it. I can now build the pulling machinery.
reaction: The cycle between ATP use and renewal was a useful connection.
reason: The thin and thick filaments appear to be the parts that make the fibre pull.
expectation: I expect them to form a filament arrangement that can slide to produce a pull, possibly needing ATP and a calcium signal to work.

alternatives.reason: Assembling the muscle fibre also seems necessary, but I want to build its pulling machinery first.

effect: The thin and thick filaments formed overlapping sliding units, which appear to be the fibre’s pulling machinery.
reaction: The arrangement makes sense, though I’m curious how it produces a pull.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should assemble the muscle fibre that will use the machinery.
expectation: I expect a muscle fibre incorporating the transporter-bearing cell boundary and its internal structures.

effect: The transporter-bearing cell and muscle structures formed a muscle fibre scaffold with spaces for contractile units.
reaction: The spaces make the next fitting clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and it should put the sliding units into the fibre.
expectation: I expect a muscle fibre containing the sliding filament units, though it may still need ATP and calcium to pull.

effect: The sliding units now fill the muscle fibre, so the ATP supply can be connected to its pulling machinery.
reaction: The fitting was predictable and made the assembly clear.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the fibre needs usable energy to pull.
expectation: I expect an energy-supplied muscle fibre, though it may still need the calcium signal before it can pull.

effect: ATP lets the myosin head release and reset, while the thin filament’s binding site remains covered. The calcium signal may make pulling possible.
reaction: The close-up makes ATP’s role more specific than simply supplying energy.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and the calcium signal appears to be the next step toward a pull.
expectation: I expect calcium to expose the binding sites so the filaments can interact and the fibre can pull.

effect: Calcium exposes grip sites, allowing myosin to pull the filaments past each other; the fibre shortens without the filaments themselves shortening.
reaction: The distinction between sliding and shortening was clear and satisfying.
reason: This is the only offered combination, and pumping calcium back into storage seems necessary for relaxation.
expectation: I expect calcium to be removed from around the filaments, allowing the binding sites to be covered again and the fibre to relax.

effect: ATP-powered pumps return calcium to storage, covering the grip sites and stopping the pull. The fibre relaxes under an outside pull and is ready to respond again.
reaction: It was interesting that relaxation also requires ATP.

mostWorthwhile.text: Adding the calcium signal was most worthwhile: the result connected the signal to myosin pulling and clearly distinguished the fibre shortening from the filaments sliding past each other.

leastWorthwhile.text: Filling the fibre with filament units was clear but predictable; it added less explanation than the later close-ups.

surprise.text: ATP helps myosin let go and reset, and also powers calcium pumps during relaxation. That made its role more specific than a general energy supply.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary. The offered combinations made their immediate purposes fairly apparent, although several steps had only one choice.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: seeing how the fibre's cellular machinery connects to larger body systems is appealing, though I would hope for more meaningful choices.
